diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The task is a Flink/Java implementation for cluster-trace analysis. The agent built, compiled, and ran successfully, but the output content did not match the expected results. The only relevant skill is senior-data-engineer, which lists Flink in its tech-stack but lacks concrete, task-specific guidance for stage/session detection semantics, exactly-matching reference output, event-time handling for microsecond timestamps, and the specific join semantics required (only emit jobs that are both finished AND have submits). The pdf skill is irrelevant (format.pdf is only read for schema reference, which the agent apparently did correctly since build/run passed).

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill advertises Flink expertise but provides no concrete guidance for implementing session-window stage detection in Flink, nor for the subtle semantics needed here: (1) counting SUBMIT events (event type 0) only, (2) using EventTimeSessionWindows with a 10-minute gap on microsecond timestamps (must convert to ms), (3) emitting one tuple per job only when the job has reached a terminal state (FINISH/FAIL/KILL and possibly not LOST), (4) correctly joining the task-session max stream with the job-finished stream so that only jobs appearing in BOTH are output, and (5) ensuring bounded-input completion flushes state via end-of-time timers. The baseline agent produced a plausible implementation that compiles and runs but mismatches the reference output, suggesting one of these semantic details (terminal-state set, SUBMIT filter, session gap boundary inclusivity, or finished-only filter) is wrong.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a Flink streaming recipes section with a worked example for 'per-key event-time session windows + terminal-state gated emission' that explicitly covers: (a) converting microsecond trace timestamps to milliseconds before assigning watermarks; (b) filtering task events to event_type==0 (SUBMIT) only, counting each SUBMIT separately (including resubmits); (c) using EventTimeSessionWindows.withGap(Time.minutes(10)) keyed by jobId and a ProcessWindowFunction to emit per-session counts; (d) reducing with keyBy(jobId).maxBy(count) to get the longest stage; (e) filtering job events to terminal states — clarify that in Google cluster-trace semantics, 'job has finished' typically means event_type in {FINISH=4} only (not FAIL/KILL/LOST), and recommend verifying against the reference; (f) joining the two streams with a KeyedCoProcessFunction that emits (jobId,count) only when BOTH the finished signal AND at least one submit-session count have arrived — never emit on timer alone if only one side appeared, so that jobs with no SUBMITs or jobs that never finished are excluded; (g) registering an end-of-input event-time timer (Long.MAX_VALUE - 1) to flush pending state on bounded sources; (h) setParallelism(1) on the sink and a single-file line writer. Include a note that output format must be exactly '(jobId,count)' with no spaces.
